source.version: Published journal article, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1910545, published 14 September 2026; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1910545 (PDF p. 1).

studies.label: Three-arm workflow experiment (argumentative essay with or without AI, then unaided parallel essay)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, abstract; PDF p. 4, Table 2, Randomized and Primary analysis sample rows (column order: Autonomous, Dependent, No-AI).
counts_source.quote: three-arm experiment (900 randomized; 659 in the primary analysis) ... Randomized 278 294 328 ... Primary analysis sample 222 225 212

arms.name: Autonomous
arms.description: Self-generation-first AI workflow: draft a thesis and outline before the AI panel unlocks, compare and question the AI points, then rewrite in own words. The later essay is unaided (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5).

arms.name: Dependent
arms.description: Direct-adoption AI workflow: generate arguments and paragraphs with AI and adopt the output with minimal changes, without a required initial outline. The later essay is unaided (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5).

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Write independently with AI tools, search engines, and external materials prohibited; the later essay is also unaided (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5).

studies.task: Write argumentative policy essays about city-center car bans and a shorter work week, first under the assigned AI or No-AI workflow and then without AI in the same session, with topic placement counterbalanced (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1; PDF p. 5, Sections 2.3-2.5).

ai_tool.name: Qwen3.5 (Tongyi Qianwen; Alibaba Cloud), official API through the study platform
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.5; the paper does not state the model release year or exact pinned version identifier.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 3, Section 2.1.1: "The study was not formally preregistered". A dated internal analysis plan preceded analysis; it is not a formal preregistration.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Phase-2 unaided reasoning quality, all arm contrasts and sensitivity specifications
not_extracted.reason: Excluded under extraction-spec rule 6 and codebook Sections 1, 6, and 13 as argumentative-writing proficiency. This is an extraction-stage classification that differs from the screening form's usefulness code. The rubric measures thesis clarity, evidence, coherence, and handling of counterarguments, and the same rubric supplies baseline writing ability (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Sections 2.6 and 2.8); it does not rate novelty or the usefulness of a creative idea. All main arm contrasts also adjust for post-treatment Phase-2 time on task (PDF p. 6, Section 2.8; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.4). This exclusion covers the robust-standard-error and individual-rater variants, additional time/effort/performance adjustments, per-protocol analyses, relaxed exclusions, available-case and multiple-imputation analyses, missing-outcome scenarios, AI-screen reinstatement, and threshold checks (PDF p. 9, Sections 3.5-3.7; PDF p. 10, Table 4). Table 4 specifies: "All models are ANCOVAs adjusting for baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task unless the speciﬁcation states otherwise".

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Phase-2 unaided idea diversity, Dependent versus No-AI, Autonomous versus No-AI, and Autonomous versus Dependent
not_extracted.reason: Extraction-spec rule 5 excludes effects adjusted for variables measured after treatment. PDF p. 6, Section 2.8 states: "For Phase-2 (transfer) models, the covariates were baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task, and for Phase-1 models, baseline ability and Phase-1 time." PDF p. 4, Table 1 note explicitly identifies "the two time-on-task rows are post-treatment". These are the adjusted contrasts in PDF p. 8, Section 3.4 and Figure 2; the additional Phase-1-time sensitivity contrast is also adjusted for a post-treatment variable (PDF p. 9, Section 3.5). The outcome is eligible in construct as within-person flexibility, but no unadjusted or baseline-only adjusted contrast is printed. The Figure 2 arm means and uncertainty are adjusted and graphical; they are not digitized.

not_extracted.what: S1: Baseline-to-Phase-2 reasoning-quality change scores in the limitations section
not_extracted.reason: Excluded under extraction-spec rule 6 and codebook Sections 1, 6, and 13 as argumentative-writing proficiency. This is an extraction-stage classification that differs from the screening form's usefulness code. The rubric measures thesis clarity, evidence, coherence, and handling of counterarguments, and the same rubric supplies baseline writing ability (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Sections 2.6 and 2.8); it does not rate novelty or the usefulness of a creative idea. PDF p. 12, Section 4.5 reports arm-level changes and an omnibus between-arm test for the same reasoning-quality rubric. This check is not excluded by assuming that it has the ANCOVA covariates: its adjustment is not stated. It is excluded on outcome scope. The omnibus test is not a pairwise contrast, and no differences or standard deviations are computed from the printed values.

not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses and direct effects conditioning on post-treatment mediators are explicitly excluded by extraction-spec rule 5 (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 3.9).

not_extracted.reason: Regressions on observed post-treatment behavior, rather than randomized-arm contrasts; they also control time on task (PDF p. 11, Section 3.10). Excluded by extraction-spec rule 5.

not_extracted.reason: Selected-subgroup and attrition descriptions rather than randomized full-sample AI contrasts (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 6, Section 2.6). Excluded by extraction-spec rule 5.

open_items: No unadjusted or baseline-only adjusted arm contrasts, raw arm means, or participant-level outcome SDs are printed for originality or within-essay idea diversity in either phase. These would be needed to extract eligible effects without conditioning on post-treatment time (PDF p. 6, Section 2.8; PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 3.2-3.4).

Figure 2 provides adjusted arm means and uncertainty graphically; no values were read off the plots. The paper does not identify a supplement supplying raw outcome statistics (PDF p. 8, Figure 2; PDF p. 13, Data availability statement).

Reasoning quality was mapped to usefulness at screening. Here its argumentative-writing-ability rubric is excluded under the extraction-stage proficiency rule, including the change-score check. This outcome classification should be reviewed in reconciliation against PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Section 2.6; and PDF p. 12, Section 4.5.

Participant residence country is not stated. The population is Chinese-speaking students and early-career workers recruited online; country is left null (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 13, Section 4.5).
Raters were trained and blind, but their professional credentials are not stated (PDF p. 6, Section 2.6).
The Qwen3.5 release year, pinned model identifier, and sampling parameter values are not printed; configuration materials are offered on request (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5).

The power paragraph reports achieved cells of 209–225, which does not match the explicit primary arm counts of 222, 225, and 212. Counts here follow the participant section and flow table, not the power paragraph (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 4, Table 2; PDF pp. 6-7, Section 2.8).

The datasets are not publicly available; de-identified data, analysis materials, instructions, and the full rubric are available only on request. No additional materials were supplied or used (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5; PDF p. 13, Data availability statement).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-11. The complete markdown was read sequentially through the references; there are no appendices in the supplied PDF. Every cited PDF page was read with pymupdf, and the participant-flow and sensitivity tables were checked with find_tables(). The randomized study is retained, but no reported effect satisfies all extraction rules. Outcome/analysis exclusions are listed separately rather than treating the experiment as non-randomized. Reasoning-quality scope is based on the rubric: "Reasoning quality captured the clarity of the thesis, the relevance and suﬃciency of evidence, the coherence of the reasoning, and the handling of counterarguments;" (PDF p. 6, Section 2.6). Within-essay idea diversity is flexibility, not across-person diversity: "idea diversity captured the number and breadth of distinct perspectives;"; originality is novelty: "originality captured novelty relative to templated answers." (same page). All reported ANCOVA effects for these eligible creativity constructs control same-phase time on task, explicitly identified as post-treatment by the paper. No adjusted effect, graphical value, or derived statistic has been entered as an eligible estimate. Assignment is between individuals; repeated tasks and counterbalanced topics do not constitute randomized within-person treatment order (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Section 2.8). The analyzed sample is the paper's modified intention-to-treat sample after exclusions (PDF p. 7, Section 2.8). Population is coded mixed for students and early-career workers; open_chat denotes interactive model access constrained by the assigned workflows (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5). No participant overlap is reported; the paper says "the present sample, which is independent of both development samples" when discussing the earlier DACOS validation samples (PDF p. 6, Section 2.7). No formal preregistered primary outcome exists; the internal plan instead names the Dependent-versus-No-AI contrast on unaided reasoning quality (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1.1).
